title: Central Vigilance Commission — Structure, Powers and Role

content.overview: The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) is the apex vigilance institution of the Union Government. It supervises vigilance administration, advises on vigilance cases and exercises statutory functions under the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.
content.glance: Identify the CVC’s statutory basis; state its principal functions (superintendence, advice, inquiry referral); note the limits relative to investigation agencies and courts.
content.study: The CVC was given statutory status by the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003 following the Supreme Court’s directions in the Vineet Narain litigation. It exercises superintendence over the Delhi Special Police Establishment (CBI) in corruption cases, advises ministries on vigilance matters, and performs other functions assigned by the Act. It does not itself try offences or replace judicial process. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in the 2003 Act and related statutory framework.

sections.heading: Statutory Basis
sections.body: Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003 confers statutory status and defines functions.

sections.heading: Superintendence and Advice
sections.body: Superintendence over CBI in corruption cases; advisory role for ministries and departments.

sections.heading: Inquiry and Referral
sections.body: Powers to inquire or cause inquiry into specified matters and to refer for further action.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.body: CVC is not a court; it does not determine criminal guilt or replace judicial review.

examples.title: Vigilance advice
examples.body: A ministry seeks CVC advice on a corruption-related disciplinary matter. The CVC’s advisory function under the 2003 Act is engaged.

hypotheticals.question: Can the CVC convict a public servant?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. It is a vigilance and supervisory body, not a criminal court.

hypotheticals.question: Does CVC superintendence oust judicial review of CBI action?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Judicial review of investigative and prosecutorial action remains available within established limits.

misconceptions.correction: It is a vigilance institution with supervisory and advisory functions.

misconceptions.trap: CVC directions completely control CBI in all matters.
misconceptions.correction: Superintendence is defined by the 2003 Act and related framework; it is not unlimited.

cases.name: Vineet Narain v Union of India
cases.facts: Directions for insulating CBI and establishing effective vigilance institutions.
cases.issue: Institutional arrangements for independent investigation of corruption.
cases.ratioDecidendi: The Court issued directions to secure independent investigation and effective vigilance oversight, leading to statutory recognition of the CVC.
cases.relevance: Foundational authority for statutory CVC status.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a CVC problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the statutory function engaged. II. State the limits of the power. III. Note relationship with CBI and courts. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Statutory basis; function; limits; relationship with investigation and review; precise relief.

examTips: Mention Vineet Narain for the institutional background.
